acceptance_criteria.text: The Event Coordinator can view pending change requests for the events assigned to them.
The Coordinator can approve or reject the requested change.

A change request covering multiple fields can be partially approved — individual fields may be accepted while others are rejected, each updating or leaving unchanged accordingly. The Event Organiser who raised the request can see each field's outcome (approved or rejected), and the Coordinator's reason for each rejected field, on the change request, and is notified of the outcome (see: Receive Event Notifications, SPM-53).

Given a change is approved, when the approval is saved, then the event information is updated and the change is applied with the same rules as a direct edit by the Coordinator (see: Update Event Information, SPM-62).
Given the event is Postponed and the approved change gives it a new date, when the approval is saved, then the new date is applied and the event moves to Approved (see: Postpone Event, SPM-38).
Rejected changes leave the existing event information unchanged.
A change request that has been approved or rejected can no longer be processed again.

test_cases.title: The coordinator's Change Requests page lists the pending requests on their own events, each with a Review link, and not processed requests or another coordinator's
test_cases.preconditions: npm run fixtures:spm32 has been run. Daniel Tan is the coordinator of every 'SPM32 …' event except 'SPM32 Other Coordinator Forum' (Priya Raj). 'SPM32 Processed Seminar' has only a request that was already processed. Logged in as daniel.tan@connectsphere.com / password123. Nothing is saved in this case.
test_cases.test_data:
Coordinator: Daniel Tan
Pending, his: SPM32 Harbour Briefing, SPM32 Confirmed Client Gala, SPM32 Postponed Product Expo, SPM32 Advisers Workshop, SPM32 Cancellation Request Forum, SPM32 Called Off Dinner, SPM32 Postponement Request Talk
Not his: SPM32 Other Coordinator Forum (Priya Raj)
Processed: SPM32 Processed Seminar
test_cases.expected_result: Step 1: The 'Change Requests' page lists a pending request for each of the seven events of the test data, each with the badge 'Pending' and a 'Review' link. 'SPM32 Processed Seminar' and 'SPM32 Other Coordinator Forum' are not listed.

Other coordinator: Priya Raj
Organiser: Rachel Ng
test_cases.expected_result:
Step 2: The page lists the request for 'SPM32 Other Coordinator Forum' and none of Daniel Tan's SPM32 events.
Step 3: The event opens with no 'Change requests' card: only the event's organisers, its assigned coordinator and the Ops Manager see its change requests (SPM-35).
Step 5: The 'Change requests' card lists the request as 'Pending' with no 'Review' link.

test_cases.title: The assigned coordinator approves some fields of a change request and rejects another with a reason, and only the approved fields change on the event
test_cases.preconditions: Run npm run fixtures:spm32 before this case. 'SPM32 Harbour Briefing' (Planning, 80 people) has a pending change request from Rachel Ng for three fields. Logged in as daniel.tan@connectsphere.com / password123. SPM-32-TC04 continues from this case, so go straight to it and run npm run fixtures:spm32 after it.
steps: Click 'Review' on the request for 'SPM32 Harbour Briefing'
For 'Event name', choose 'Reject' and enter the reason
test_cases.test_data:
Event: SPM32 Harbour Briefing
Event name: SPM32 Harbour Briefing -> SPM32 Harbour Briefing and Lunch (reject; reason: The invitations have already gone out under the current name.)
Expected attendance: 80 -> 110 (approve)
Description: Quarterly briefing for wealth clients. -> Quarterly briefing with a networking lunch. (approve)
test_cases.expected_result:
Step 2: The 'Review change request' page shows the request's reason 'More clients have confirmed and we are adding lunch.' and one row per field - Event name, Description, Expected attendance - each with its current and proposed value and the choices 'Approve' and 'Reject', with 'Approve all', 'Reject all' and 'Save decision'.
Step 3: A 'Reason for rejecting' box appears under Event name.
Step 5: A green alert 'Change request processed.' is shown with the badge 'Partly approved', and each field's outcome: Event name 'Rejected', Expected attendance and Description 'Approved'.
Step 6: The event's title is still 'SPM32 Harbour Briefing'. Expected attendance reads 110 and the description 'Quarterly briefing with a networking lunch.'

open_questions: DECIDED 2026-10-25: the coordinator reviews a request on 'Review change request' at /events/<reference>/change-requests/<request> (UI_DESIGN.md S-17), reached by a 'Review' link on each pending request on the Change Requests page and on the event's Change requests card - shown only to the event's assigned coordinator.

DECIDED 2026-10-25: a change of details is decided item by item - each changed field, and the equipment change if there is one - with 'Approve' / 'Reject' for each, 'Approve all' and 'Reject all' to set them all, and 'Save decision'. A rejected item needs a 'Reason for rejecting' ('Give a reason for rejecting <field>.'). Every item must be decided ('Approve or reject every change before saving.').

DECIDED 2026-10-25: the request's status after a decision is 'Approved' (all items approved), 'Rejected' (all rejected) or 'Partly approved' (status value partially_approved). The page then shows 'Change request processed.' with each item's outcome. The Change requests card (organiser and coordinator) adds an Outcome column - 'Approved' or 'Rejected: <reason>' - and 'Processed by <name> on <date, time>'.

DECIDED 2026-10-25: approved fields are applied with Update Event Information's rules (applyEventInformation, SPM-62): important changes flag arrangements, a Confirmed (or Safety review / Safety approved) event goes back to Planning, and the coordinator is asked first with SPM-62's own dialog ('Move this event back to Planning?', 'Save and move to Planning' / 'Keep editing'). Arrangements flagged are listed under 'Flagged for review', as on Edit event information.
DECIDED 2026-10-25: an approved equipment change is recorded but not applied - it is free text - and the result says 'Update the Equipment tab to match the approved equipment change.'

DECIDED 2026-10-25 (AC5): for a Postponed event, the approved fields are applied and, if Starts at or Ends at is among them, the event moves to Approved (status history 'Rescheduled: change request approved'); the page notes it first and says 'The event has moved from Postponed to Approved.' afterwards. Other approved fields on a Postponed event are applied and it stays Postponed.

DECIDED 2026-10-25: approving is refused once the event is closed ('This event is <status>, so its changes can no longer be approved.'); rejecting is still allowed. The approved fields together must still make sense: an end before the start is refused ('With these decisions the event would end before it starts. Decide Starts at and Ends at together.'), as is a start before registration closes (SPM-62's message).

DECIDED 2026-10-25 (user, 2026-10-25): postponement and cancellation requests are processed by Postpone Event (SPM-38) and Cancel Event (SPM-37). Here they can be rejected with a reason ('Reject request'). A cancellation request is approved by cancelling the event: Cancel event now marks a pending cancellation request Approved (its dialog lists 'Approve 1 cancellation request') and closes other pending requests as before. A postponement request can only be rejected until SPM-38 is built.

DECIDED 2026-10-25 (AC7): the decision is saved only if the request is still Pending (checked in the database, so two coordinators' saves at once decide it once); otherwise 'This change request has already been processed.' A processed request opens read-only and leaves the Change Requests page.

DECIDED 2026-10-25: proposed values are applied as the request stored them, even if the event changed since. Requests made before SPM-35 (proposed start, end or attendance only) are decided the same way.

RESOLVED 2026-10-25: notifying the organiser of the outcome (AC3's 'is notified of the outcome') belongs to Receive Event Notifications (SPM-53, In Progress), per the 2026-09-18 and 2026-10-18 comments. SPM-32 writes no notifications; no case for it.

RESOLVED 2026-10-25: identifying and flagging affected arrangements and reverting a Confirmed event are SPM-62's rules, reused here (comment 2026-10-04), so TC07 checks them only as the effect of an approval.
